name: 瓦斯科·达·伽马

points.title: 早年航海训练
points.description: 瓦斯科·达·伽马出生于葡萄牙锡尼什的一个贵族家庭，父亲埃斯特旺·达·伽马也是一位经验丰富的航海家。在这个葡萄牙航海黄金时代，达·伽马接受了系统的航海训练，学习了航海技术、天文学和地理知识。葡萄牙当时正处于亨利王子开创的航海探索传统中，这为达·伽马后来的航海事业奠定了坚实基础。他在这一时期积累了丰富的航海经验，并熟悉了葡萄牙王室对寻找通往印度海路的重视。
points.descriptionEn: Born into a noble family in Sines, Portugal, Vasco da Gama received comprehensive maritime training during Portugal's Age of Discovery. His father, Estêvão da Gama, was an experienced navigator. Under the influence of Prince Henry's maritime exploration tradition, da Gama acquired skills in navigation, astronomy, and geography. This period laid the foundation for his future voyages, as he became familiar with Portugal's royal emphasis on finding a sea route to India.

points.title: 首次印度航行
points.description: 1497年7月8日，达·伽马受葡萄牙国王曼努埃尔一世派遣，率领四艘船从里斯本出发，开始寻找通往印度的海上航线。他绕过非洲好望角，首次成功开辟了欧洲至印度的直接海路。1498年5月20日，他抵达印度卡利卡特，成为首位从欧洲经由海路到达印度的航海家。这次航行历时近两年，虽然与当地统治者贸易谈判并不顺利，但达·伽马带回了珍贵的香料和货物，证明了欧洲与亚洲直接贸易的可能性，为葡萄牙在东方建立贸易帝国奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: On July 8, 1497, da Gama departed from Lisbon with four ships, commissioned by King Manuel I of Portugal to find a sea route to India. He successfully rounded the Cape of Good Hope and became the first European to reach India by sea, arriving at Calicut on May 20, 1498. Although trade negotiations with local rulers were difficult, his nearly two-year voyage proved the feasibility of direct European-Asian trade and laid the foundation for Portugal's trading empire in the East.

points.title: 第二次印度远征
points.description: 1502年，达·伽马率领由二十艘船组成的庞大舰队再次前往印度，这次他不仅是探险家，更是葡萄牙在印度洋的军事指挥官。他采取了更为强硬的手段，摧毁了阿拉伯商船，迫使印度沿海城市屈服于葡萄牙的贸易控制。在这次航行中，达·伽马建立了葡萄牙在印度科钦和果阿的贸易站，并成功垄断了香料贸易。他的军事行动和贸易政策使葡萄牙在印度洋地区确立了霸权地位，但也因其暴力手段和对当地文化的破坏而备受争议。
points.descriptionEn: In 1502, da Gama led a fleet of twenty ships on his second voyage to India, this time as a military commander. He employed more aggressive tactics, destroying Arab merchant ships and forcing Indian coastal cities to submit to Portuguese trade control. He established trading posts in Cochin and Goa, effectively monopolizing the spice trade. While establishing Portuguese dominance in the Indian Ocean, his violent methods and cultural destruction remain controversial.

points.title: 印度总督
points.description: 1524年，达·伽马被任命为葡萄牙在印度的第二任总督，被派往整顿葡萄牙在东方的殖民事务。他抵达果阿后，立即着手改革殖民 administration，打击腐败，并试图改善与当地统治者的关系。然而，他的任期非常短暂，同年12月24日，他在果阿去世，享年约55岁。达·伽马的死亡标志着一个时代的结束，但他作为开辟欧亚海上航线的先驱，其历史功绩不可磨灭。他被安葬在果阿，后遗体于1539年被运回葡萄牙，现安葬于里斯本的热罗尼莫斯修道院。
points.descriptionEn: In 1524, da Gama was appointed as the second Viceroy of India, tasked with reforming Portuguese colonial affairs in the East. Upon arriving in Goa, he began administrative reforms, fighting corruption, and attempting to improve relations with local rulers. However, his tenure was brief, as he died in Goa on December 24, 1524, at approximately age 55. His death marked the end of an era, but his legacy as the pioneer of the sea route between Europe and Asia remains significant.

points.title: 历史纪念
points.description: 达·伽马逝世三百多年后，葡萄牙为纪念这位伟大的航海家，在里斯本的热罗尼莫斯修道院为他建造了宏伟的陵墓。1880年，葡萄牙举行了盛大的纪念活动，将达·伽马的遗骨重新安葬于此。修道院本身就是葡萄牙航海时代的象征，与达·伽马的历史功绩相得益彰。此外，里斯本还有以他命名的达·伽马大桥和达·伽马塔，这些纪念建筑成为葡萄牙民族自豪感的象征，也反映了达·伽马在葡萄牙历史中的重要地位。
points.descriptionEn: Over 300 years after his death, Portugal honored the great navigator with a magnificent tomb in the Jerónimos Monastery in Lisbon. In 1880, Portugal held grand commemorative events, reinterring da Gama's remains at this site. The monastery itself symbolizes Portugal's Age of Discovery, complementing da Gama's historical achievements. Lisbon also features the Vasco da Gama Bridge and Tower, monuments that symbolize Portuguese national pride and reflect da Gama's significant place in the country's history.

supporter.zh: 达·伽马被誉为伟大的航海家和开拓者，他的航行开辟了欧洲与亚洲直接贸易的海上通道，打破了阿拉伯商人对香料贸易的垄断。他展示了葡萄牙航海技术的卓越成就，为葡萄牙建立了庞大的殖民贸易帝国奠定了基础。支持者认为达·伽马代表了人类探索精神和勇气，他的航行促进了东西方文化交流，开启了全球化进程的序幕。
supporter.en: Da Gama is celebrated as a great navigator and pioneer whose voyages established direct maritime trade between Europe and Asia, breaking the Arab monopoly on spice trade. Supporters argue he demonstrated exceptional Portuguese maritime skill and laid the foundation for Portugal's vast colonial trading empire. They view him as a symbol of human exploration and courage, whose voyages facilitated cultural exchange between East and West, heralding the dawn of globalization.

critic.zh: 批评者指出达·伽马的航行伴随着暴力和文化破坏，他在印度洋地区的军事行动导致许多无辜者死亡，破坏了当地商业网络。他的殖民扩张体现了欧洲帝国主义的掠夺本质，为后来的殖民剥削树立了先例。达·伽马对当地文化的漠视和强制贸易政策被视为早期殖民主义的典型代表，其历史遗产包含着对非欧洲文明的征服与压迫。
critic.en: Critics highlight that da Gama's voyages were accompanied by violence and cultural destruction. His military actions in the Indian Ocean resulted in numerous deaths and disruption of local commercial networks. His colonial expansion is seen as embodying the exploitative nature of European imperialism, setting precedents for later colonial exploitation. Da Gama's disregard for local cultures and coercive trade policies are viewed as typical examples of early colonialism, with his legacy including the conquest and oppression of non-European civilizations.

objective.zh: 从历史角度看，达·伽马是地理大发现时代的关键人物，他的航行改变了世界贸易格局，促进了全球连接。他既是开拓者也是殖民者，其历史地位体现了探索精神与殖民扩张的双重性。在流行文化中，达·伽马常被象征为欧洲扩张时代的代表，他的故事反映了人类历史上的重大转折点——从区域文明向全球互动的转变。历史学界普遍承认他的航行具有划时代意义，同时也对其殖民遗产持批判态度。
objective.en: Historically, da Gama stands as a pivotal figure in the Age of Discovery whose voyages transformed global trade patterns and increased worldwide connectivity. He embodies both explorer and colonizer, reflecting the dual nature of the expansionist era. In popular culture, he symbolizes European expansion, with his story representing a major historical turning point from regional civilizations to global interaction. Historians generally acknowledge the epochal significance of his voyages while maintaining a critical perspective on his colonial legacy.

self.zh: 我们发现了通往印度的航线，这是葡萄牙王国的荣耀。
self.en: We have found the way to India, which is the glory of the Kingdom of Portugal.

others.zh: 达·伽马是历史上最伟大的航海家之一，他不仅开辟了新航线，更开启了欧洲与亚洲直接交流的时代。
others.en: Da Gama was one of the greatest navigators in history, not only opening new sea routes but also initiating an era of direct European-Asian interaction.

othersBy: 葡萄牙历史学家若泽·萨拉查
